external_entities.name: Duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The text does not describe how the engineer signs in.

external_entities.name: Scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state how the partner identifies the importer.

processes.name: Dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers in a browser.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: The text does not state how an engineer signs in to it, which origins the API allows through CORS, or whether CORS allows credentials.

processes.name: Corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it
processes.notes: Serving the console does not establish the host's trust-zone placement.

processes.name: Dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The API is served cross-origin to the console. The text does not state its authentication mechanism.

processes.name: Schedule importer
processes.description: A process that pulls and parses the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, archives downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token to the dispatch API. The token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: Dispatch database
data_stores.description: The database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Each job order carries the token or session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. The text does not state how the database is protected at rest.

data_stores.name: Schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store containing each document downloaded from the scheduling partner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_stores.notes: The text does not state the archive's trust-zone placement or protection at rest.

data_stores.name: Corporate file store
data_stores.description: The file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store
data_stores.notes: The text identifies the file store as the location of the archive but does not state its trust-zone placement or protection at rest.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state the browser transport or authentication details.

data_flows.name: serve console
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. The allowed origins and whether credentials are allowed were not recorded.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after opening.

data_flows.name: read and write database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and token or session data

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed every hour over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: The text does not state how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write schedule archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The importer presents an API token. The token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.notes: The schedule importer is also stated to run on this network.

trust_boundaries.name: Production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate, where an account can move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet and holds more authority than a corporate laptop.

trust_boundaries.name: Another company
trust_boundaries.description: The company that controls the scheduling partner.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's contents are confidential because it holds crew mobile numbers and token or session data.
assumptions.basis: The database is stated to hold crew mobile numbers and the token or session that created each job order.
